newsitem.title: USA: ACE one of Telstar 401 insurers.
newsitem.headline: ACE one of Telstar 401 insurers.

text.p: ACE Ltd said it was one of the insurers of AT&T Corp's Telstar 401 satellite, which stopped operating on Saturday.
AT&T earlier said it was unsuccessful in attempting to re-establish contact with Telstar 401 and has declared the satellite permanently out of service.
AT&T declined to say how much the satellite was worth. AT&T also declined to say exactly how much insurance it had on the satellite, but said the coverage was substantial.
Satellites generally cost at least $150 million when new, an industry source said.
The Telstar 401 satellite, however, was launched in December 1993, making it about three years old and somewhat less valuable than it was when new, the source said.
Bermuda-based ACE declined to say what its share of the in-orbit insurance coverage was or how large its loss might be.
"It hurt, but it didn't kill us," an ACE spokeswoman said.

Other major satellite insurers include Munich Re, Assicurazioni Generali SpA, Lloyd's of London, International Technology Underwriters in Washington D.C. and U.S. Aviation Insurance Group, an industry source said.

AT&T's Telstar 402 satellite, which failed after it was deployed from an Ariane rocket in September 1994, resulted in a $187 million claim, according to a report in insurance trade publication Business Insurance.

The news of the failure of the Telstar 401 satellite came just shortly before an unmanned Delta II rocket carrying a $40 million U.S. Air Force navigational satellite exploded after take-off in Florida.
McDonnell Douglas Corp was the maker of the Delta II and a division of Boeing Co built the rocket's engine.
The Delta II was the same type of rocket that was to launch three Iridium LLC satellites on Monday.
Iridium late Friday said that launch will be delayed because of the rocket explosion in Florida.
The cost of launch rockets can range anywhere from $30 million to $120 million, with most averaging around $50 million, an industry source said.
The Delta II's value could not be immediately determined.
